claims.claim_vi: A chat message goes from the sending application in user space to the send buffer in kernel space, is wrapped with a TCP header, an IP header and a MAC header, goes through qdisc for flow control and reaches the NIC via a ring buffer.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: The NIC sends the data over the internet through routers and switches to the NIC of the receiving server.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: The receiving NIC puts the data in the ring buffer and sends a hard interrupt to the CPU; the CPU sends a soft interrupt so ksoftirqd receives data from the ring buffer; the data is unwrapped through the data link, network and transport layers and copied to user space.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: qdisc and ksoftirqd are Linux kernel names: the Linux kernel source has a per-CPU ksoftirqd task and qdisc code.
